content.content: Launching skill: git-worktree-pr

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/skills/git-worktree-pr

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
  price of the directory being inside the repo.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

**The repository is public since 2026-09-06**, which is what makes GitHub-side
enforcement possible at all: a private repo on a free personal plan answers
`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` on both
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` — that was the prior state, and it is not a
description to trust going forward if the repo ever goes private again. Do not
cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting `"protected":
false` as proof of anything either way: that field only ever reflects legacy
branch protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and it read `false`
on the free-private plan whatever the configuration. Query
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` itself (or `gh ruleset check main`) for the
real answer.

A ruleset named `main-protection` (id `22399372`) now targets `refs/heads/main`
only — deliberately not `entire/checkpoints/v1`, which receives automatic
pushes from the Entire hook and would break if rule-gated. It requires a pull
request (0 approving reviews — solo maintainer, the PR is a record not a review
gate) with the `Lint and build` and `Test` checks from `ci.yml` passing,
blocks force-pushes and branch deletion, and grants no bypass. This closes the
gap the mirror alone left open: the Entire mirror's rejection of a direct push
to `main` was, until now, the *only* protection — a second remote pointing
straight at GitHub would have sailed through (see the warning against adding
one, below). Now GitHub itself refuses that push too.

**The `Entire Gates` check is expected to stay red on this repository.** It is
a PR check from the `entire` app, and its **Approvals** gate fails until another
reviewer approves the trail. That approval cannot arrive: the repository has one
developer, so the gate cannot be green, and no second account or dummy reviewer
should be added to satisfy it. The check is not required by `main-protection`
(GitHub reports the PR as `UNSTABLE` but `MERGEABLE`), so a red `Entire Gates`
alone does not block a merge. Merge once `Lint and build` and `Test` pass. The
Findings, Checks and Up to date gates must stay green: if any of them fails, it
is a real signal, so stop and raise it with the user. Agents (orchestrator,
devops) must not stop to ask for agreement over the Approvals failure alone.
To read the reason:
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="Entire Gates") | .output.summary'`.

Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
and is forwarded to GitHub.

**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.

```bash
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
# then, from the main checkout:
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
```

**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.

**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.

**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** The
`main-protection` ruleset (above) would now refuse a direct `git push github
main` too, so it is no longer the *only* defeat of the only protection — but a
direct push still bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that
records checkpoints and sessions, which is not visible until much later.
`origin` is the only remote, deliberately.

**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.


**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
```

### Remotes

| Remote | URL | Use |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |

**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on
GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1` (a second placement exists
in `aws-us-east-2`), but every git operation goes through the mirror: it is the
regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint
hook runs. Anything needing GitHub's own answer — PR state, review threads —
goes through `gh`, which authenticates directly and does not need a remote.

Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
fixes this.

The sandbox/host relay (landing a sandbox-made commit, developing in the sandbox and testing from the host) is in [sandbox.md](sandbox.md); read it only when a sandbox is involved.

After the merge, load the `release-flow` skill.

- Depuis /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk : `git fetch origin main && git worktree add -b spike/view-cursor .worktrees/spike/view-cursor origin/main`, puis travaille UNIQUEMENT dans ce worktree. Seulement la palette `ctrl+p` et la FilterBar. Aucun autre champ de formulaire. Une durée bornée : une à deux sessions, ne t'enlise pas.

1. Champ focalisé (palette ou FilterBar) : à la composition de la frame finale, le curseur matériel est placé sur la cellule de saisie. - Régressions de position constatées (largeur de caractères larges/emoji/combinants, texte plus long que le champ, défilement horizontal du champ, redimensionnement, 80x24).

Résultat (marche / ne marche pas / marche avec réserves), branche et commit, fichiers touchés, mesures chiffrées, risques, recommandation GO ou NO-GO argumentée, points ouverts. Ne fais pas de narration. Ne mets rien dans `docs/backlog.md` : la décision sera consignée à part par l'orchestrateur.

  ## SPIKE DEVDESK-294: hardware cursor for the `ctrl+p` palette and the FilterBar
  
  **Result: works, with reservations.** Position, text and fallback are verified by tests at 80x24, 120x40, 60x30 and 40x16. Nothing was run in a real terminal.
  
  **Branch and commit:** `spike/view-cursor`, commit `142e9e96`. Worktree: `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.worktrees/spike/view-cursor`. Committed locally only: nothing pushed, no PR, `docs/backlog.md` untouched.
  
  ### Files touched
  Paths are relative to `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.worktrees/spike/view-cursor/`.
  - `internal/ui/components/cursor_marker.go` (new): `InputView`, `ResolveCursor`, `StripCursor`, and the gate `SetTerminalCursor` (a package-level atomic, **off by default**).
  - `internal/ui/components/filter_bar.go`: one line, `fb.searchInput.View()` becomes `InputView(fb.searchInput)`.
  - `internal/app/command_suggestions.go`: `paletteInputView` ends with `components.InputView(in)`.
  - `internal/app/view.go`: `View()` resolves the markers and sets `v.Cursor`. `Render()` still returns the stripped frame, split into `render()` + `Render()`. `withPalette` calls `StripCursor` on the screen under the palette.
  - Tests: `internal/app/spike_cursor_test.go` and `internal/ui/components/cursor_marker_test.go`. Keys come from `testutil`; there is no literal `tea.KeyPressMsg`.
  
  ### Mechanism
  - The focused field renders its text with the virtual cursor hidden and leaves a zero-width APC marker in front of the cursor cell. The marker carries the shape, blink and colour, plus the cell drawn both ways: A with the virtual cursor, B without it.
  - `ResolveCursor` runs on the final frame. It requires exactly one marker, whose B cell must still follow it intact, and X < width.
    - Resolved: it strips the marker and sets `View.Cursor` at (x, y), with X taken from `ansi.StringWidth`.
    - Unresolved for any reason: it swaps marker+B for A, so the virtual cursor stays. This gives criterion 3 without the router ever touching `SetVirtualCursor`. The decision is made on the final frame, so there is no second render.
  - A palette open over a focused FilterBar: `StripCursor` removes the underlying marker, so only the palette owns the cursor.
  - With an overlay open (help, context list), `Render()` returns the overlay only, so the cursor is nil.
  
  ### Why not `textinput.Cursor()`
  `Cursor()` in bubbles v2.2.1 is not usable here. It counts runes, not cells, and ignores the private scroll offset.
  
  Measured against the marker column:
  
  | Case | `textinput.Cursor().X` agrees? |
  |---|---|
  | ASCII | yes |
  | CJK | no (3 vs 6) |
  | emoji | no (2 vs 4) |
  | scrolled, cursor in the middle | no (10 vs 7) |
  | combining marks | no (4 vs 2) |
  
  So the column is found by rendering the input twice (cursor drawn, cursor hidden) and diffing the two strings. Both renders are made on copies.
  - Calling `Focus()` on a copy would cancel the live model's blink timer through the shared `blinkCtx`. I avoided it.
  - The visible render uses a static cursor style, so it works during the blink-off phase.
  
  ### Tests (observed)
  - **Palette, text and position:** the stripped frame is identical to the spike-free frame. The cursor X matches the expected column for "", ASCII, CJK, combining marks and VS16 emoji.
  - **Palette against an oracle:** the oracle is the virtual cursor cell located with `testutil.Cells` in the spike-free frame. Cursor X/Y matched on scrolled ASCII, scrolled CJK, and after `left`/`home`/`end`/`right` moves. Not checkable by the oracle: combining marks and the ZWJ family emoji. For combining marks the virtual cursor cell has zero width, so there is no oracle; the cursor was resolved at plausible columns but I have not verified them.
  - **FilterBar:** correct X/Y at 80x24, 120x40 and 40x16, including CJK.
  - **No focus / overlay / palette over a focused bar:** cursor nil, nil, and the palette's only, respectively.
  - **Fallback:** a cut cell, two markers, an out-of-bounds marker and a too-narrow palette all give a nil cursor and the virtual-cursor frame. Compared by cells, not bytes: a clipped cell can leave an empty SGR byte difference.
  
  ### Position regressions found
  All of the following are unresolved cases (nil cursor, virtual-cursor fallback), not wrong positions:
  1. **VS16 emoji (`❤️`) in the palette at 40 columns.** textinput measures with runewidth (❤ = 1 cell) while `x/ansi` and lipgloss count 2. The text overflows, `inputRow` truncates it, and the cursor cell is clipped. Unresolved, and the virtual cursor is invisible in that case too.
  2. **Shrinking the terminal while the palette holds long text** (120x40 to 40x16). The input keeps its old scroll window and the cursor cell leaves the row. This is pre-existing: the virtual cursor is already invisible. Unresolved, so no regression, but a real cursor cannot fix it without a re-seat in `Update`.
  3. **FilterBar never sets a width on its `textinput`.** There is no horizontal scroll, and a long query overruns `BarFrame`. A query under the width resolves correctly (100 `x` at 120 columns); on a narrower terminal the cell goes off-screen and falls back. This is pre-existing.
  4. **Combining marks.** textinput puts the cursor between the base letter and the mark. The virtual cell is then a lone zero-width mark.
  5. **Width of the marker itself.** It is zero cells for `ansi.StringWidth`, `lipgloss.Width`, `theme.PadWithBg`, `ansi.Strip` and `Style.Width(...).Render`.
     - `ansi.Truncate` and `ansi.Cut` keep the marker even when they clip its cell. The "B cell must follow" check is therefore required, not optional.
     - `ansi.Wrap` keeps it.
  6. **Rule 119.** The guard `TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo` rejected a decoded `color.RGBA`. I switched to `lipgloss.Color("#"+hex)`; the guard passes.
  
  I did not test placeholder text (empty value with a placeholder): neither surface uses one.
  
  ### Cost of `View()` (120x40, `go test -bench`, `-count=3`; gate off is the pre-spike cost plus one atomic load)
  
  | Case | Off | On | Delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | palette | 810–838 µs, 260 KB, 3436 allocs | 877–919 µs, 281 KB, 3498 allocs | about +6%, +62 allocs |
  | FilterBar | 531–544 µs, 189 KB, 2707 allocs | 550–572 µs, 205 KB, 2754 allocs | about +5%, +47 allocs |
  | idle (no field) | 529–538 µs | 532–549 µs | noise |
  | `InputView` alone, short | 5.3 µs | 11.8 µs | 2.2x |
  | `InputView` alone, scrolled | 7.2 µs | 15 µs | 2.1x |
  
  The full `View()` is already about 0.5 ms idle. The extra is about 50 µs on screen when a field is focused, which is acceptable.
  
  ### Not verifiable from an agent
  - Windows Terminal, WSL and conhost behaviour with `View.Cursor`.
  - Real cursor shapes and blink, terminal colour handling, and what the IME and screen readers actually track. I only checked the `tea.Cursor` struct we set.
  - Whether the hide/show escapes bubbletea emits behave on terminals that ignore them, and cursor flicker during redraw.
  - APC handling by tmux/screen/terminals. The marker is stripped before sending, so nothing leaves the process; but my claim that the program never emits it is based on the tests only, not on a captured byte stream.
  - The existing virtual-cursor blink versus a terminal-driven blink.
  
  ### Remaining work to generalise
  - **Per-widget capability instead of the global gate** (a flag passed to the field, set from config `app.cursor: virtual|terminal`): S.
  - **Other fields.** `WrappedInput` (Rule 133) draws its own cursor, so it needs the same marker, adapted rather than replaced. Wrapped lines make X/Y depend on the wrap: M. The remaining `textinput` forms: M.

- The focused field renders its text with the virtual cursor hidden and leaves a zero-width APC marker in front of the cursor cell. The marker carries the shape, blink and colour, plus the cell drawn both ways: A with the virtual cursor, B without it.

  - Resolved: it strips the marker and sets `View.Cursor` at (x, y), with X taken from `ansi.StringWidth`.
  - Unresolved for any reason: it swaps marker+B for A, so the virtual cursor stays. This gives criterion 3 without the router ever touching `SetVirtualCursor`. The decision is made on the final frame, so there is no second render.

- With an overlay open (help, context list), `Render()` returns the overlay only, so the cursor is nil.

`Cursor()` in bubbles v2.2.1 is not usable here. It counts runes, not cells, and ignores the private scroll offset.

Measured against the marker column:

| Case | `textinput.Cursor().X` agrees? |
|---|---|
| ASCII | yes |
| CJK | no (3 vs 6) |
| emoji | no (2 vs 4) |
| scrolled, cursor in the middle | no (10 vs 7) |
| combining marks | no (4 vs 2) |

So the column is found by rendering the input twice (cursor drawn, cursor hidden) and diffing the two strings. Both renders are made on copies.
- Calling `Focus()` on a copy would cancel the live model's blink timer through the shared `blinkCtx`. I avoided it.
- The visible render uses a static cursor style, so it works during the blink-off phase.

- **Palette, text and position:** the stripped frame is identical to the spike-free frame. The cursor X matches the expected column for "", ASCII, CJK, combining marks and VS16 emoji.
- **Palette against an oracle:** the oracle is the virtual cursor cell located with `testutil.Cells` in the spike-free frame. Cursor X/Y matched on scrolled ASCII, scrolled CJK, and after `left`/`home`/`end`/`right` moves. Not checkable by the oracle: combining marks and the ZWJ family emoji. For combining marks the virtual cursor cell has zero width, so there is no oracle; the cursor was resolved at plausible columns but I have not verified them.
- **FilterBar:** correct X/Y at 80x24, 120x40 and 40x16, including CJK.
- **No focus / overlay / palette over a focused bar:** cursor nil, nil, and the palette's only, respectively.
- **Fallback:** a cut cell, two markers, an out-of-bounds marker and a too-narrow palette all give a nil cursor and the virtual-cursor frame. Compared by cells, not bytes: a clipped cell can leave an empty SGR byte difference.

### Position regressions found
All of the following are unresolved cases (nil cursor, virtual-cursor fallback), not wrong positions:
1. **VS16 emoji (`❤️`) in the palette at 40 columns.** textinput measures with runewidth (❤ = 1 cell) while `x/ansi` and lipgloss count 2. The text overflows, `inputRow` truncates it, and the cursor cell is clipped. Unresolved, and the virtual cursor is invisible in that case too.
2. **Shrinking the terminal while the palette holds long text** (120x40 to 40x16). The input keeps its old scroll window and the cursor cell leaves the row. This is pre-existing: the virtual cursor is already invisible. Unresolved, so no regression, but a real cursor cannot fix it without a re-seat in `Update`.
3. **FilterBar never sets a width on its `textinput`.** There is no horizontal scroll, and a long query overruns `BarFrame`. A query under the width resolves correctly (100 `x` at 120 columns); on a narrower terminal the cell goes off-screen and falls back. This is pre-existing.
4. **Combining marks.** textinput puts the cursor between the base letter and the mark. The virtual cell is then a lone zero-width mark.
5. **Width of the marker itself.** It is zero cells for `ansi.StringWidth`, `lipgloss.Width`, `theme.PadWithBg`, `ansi.Strip` and `Style.Width(...).Render`.

   - `ansi.Wrap` keeps it.
6. **Rule 119.** The guard `TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo` rejected a decoded `color.RGBA`. I switched to `lipgloss.Color("#"+hex)`; the guard passes.

| Case | Off | On | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| palette | 810–838 µs, 260 KB, 3436 allocs | 877–919 µs, 281 KB, 3498 allocs | about +6%, +62 allocs |
| FilterBar | 531–544 µs, 189 KB, 2707 allocs | 550–572 µs, 205 KB, 2754 allocs | about +5%, +47 allocs |
| idle (no field) | 529–538 µs | 532–549 µs | noise |
| `InputView` alone, short | 5.3 µs | 11.8 µs | 2.2x |
| `InputView` alone, scrolled | 7.2 µs | 15 µs | 2.1x |

- Windows Terminal, WSL and conhost behaviour with `View.Cursor`.

content.text:
Le spike de la 294 est fait. Il marche, avec des réserves, et il n'a été testé que par des tests automatisés. La 212 est annulée, avec un commentaire dans Plane. La 294 est en In Progress.

J'ai relancé le build et les tests ciblés du curseur dans `internal/ui/components` et `internal/app` : ils passent. Le commit est `142e9e96`, sur la branche `spike/view-cursor`, en local seulement. Il n'y a pas de push, pas de PR, et `docs/backlog.md` n'est pas touché.

**Ce qui a été fait :**
- Le champ insère un marqueur invisible de largeur nulle. Le routeur le repère dans la frame finale, calcule la position et l'envoie au terminal.
- Si la position n'est pas sûre, le curseur virtuel actuel reste affiché, comme aujourd'hui.
- Quand la palette est ouverte, elle prend le curseur. Avec un overlay ouvert, ou sans champ focalisé, il n'y a pas de curseur matériel.
- Des tests vérifient la position et le texte inchangé à 80x24, 120x40, 60x30 et 40x16.
- Le coût de `View()` est de **+5 à 6 %** (environ 50 µs) quand un champ est focalisé, et nul sinon.

**Pourquoi pas `textinput.Cursor()` :** il se trompe pour le chinois, les emoji, le texte défilé et les accents combinés. Le coder a donc retrouvé la colonne en comparant deux rendus du champ, curseur dessiné et curseur caché. C'est un palliatif, qui double le rendu du champ.

**Réserves :**
- Un emoji comme `❤️` dans la palette à 40 colonnes n'est pas résolu : `textinput` le compte pour 1 cellule, `x/ansi` pour 2. Le repli sur le curseur virtuel s'applique, mais celui-ci est aussi invisible dans ce cas.
- La FilterBar n'a pas de défilement horizontal. Une requête plus large que le terminal donne un curseur non résolu.
- Après un rétrécissement de la fenêtre avec du texte long dans la palette, le curseur est perdu. Le curseur virtuel l'est déjà aujourd'hui.
- Windows Terminal, WSL, les formes et le clignotement réels, et la gestion d'APC par tmux n'ont pas été testés. C'est à toi de les vérifier.
- Un finding lint mineur (QF1008) reste dans un test du spike.

**Recommandation du coder : GO conditionnel**, en opt-in avec `app.cursor: virtual` par défaut. Il pose trois conditions : un test manuel dans Windows Terminal et WSL, les correctifs de largeur (surtout les emoji), et une vraie source pour la colonne du curseur à la place de la comparaison de deux rendus. Une généralisation coûterait au moins M : `WrappedInput` (Rule 133), les autres champs de saisie, la gestion du réglage et la documentation.

Mon avis : le gain est surtout visuel (forme, couleur, plus de trou de fond). Tu as déjà écarté l'accessibilité et l'IME, donc le GO vaut surtout si le rendu du curseur te gêne aujourd'hui.

Qu'est-ce que tu décides ?
1. **GO.** Je consigne la décision dans `docs/backlog.md` via une PR docs séparée, et je crée la story de généralisation en Backlog. Je clos la 294.
2. **NO-GO.** Je consigne la décision et les mesures dans `docs/backlog.md`, je clos la 294 et je laisse la branche en local.
3. **Tester d'abord à la main.** Je te donne la marche à suivre pour lancer le build du spike dans Windows Terminal et WSL, et la 294 reste en cours.
